q: A presiding officer treats a group of one-third of a party's members as protected by a split. Which statement is correct?
options: The split defence was deleted in 2003 and the members are liable to disqualification
The split defence continues and the members are protected from disqualification
The split defence continues but requires the prior approval of the Election Commission
The split defence was deleted in 1985 when the Schedule was first inserted
expl: Only a merger now operates as a defence; the split defence was removed in 2003.
why: The fourth option gives the right conclusion with a wrong date, which recognition alone will not catch.
trapnote: Merger survives, split does not. The deletion came in 2003, not at the outset.

q: Consider the 2022 decision on the economic reservation: 1-It upheld the amendment. 2-It held the ceiling not to be part of the basic structure. 3-It held that economic criteria alone cannot support reservation. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It held that economic criteria alone may support reservation.
why: The third statement inverts a central holding, which is why it reads plausibly to a candidate recalling the controversy.
trapnote: The decision permitted economic criteria alone and released that quota from the ceiling.

q: A law is placed in the Ninth Schedule in 1980 and is challenged in 2020. Which statement is correct?
options: It may not be challenged, the Schedule affording absolute protection to laws within it
It may be challenged only on grounds of legislative competence
It may be challenged for damaging the basic structure, having been inserted after April 1973
It may be challenged for damaging the basic structure, the cut-off being the year 1951
expl: Laws inserted after the 1973 decision are open to basic-structure challenge.
why: The fourth option gives the right principle with the wrong cut-off, which is a single-word variation.
trapnote: The cut-off is April 1973, the date of the decision that established the doctrine.

q: Consider a Bill amending the article that contains the amending power itself. Which statement is correct?
options: It requires a special majority alone, the article being outside the federal list
It requires a special majority and ratification by not less than half the State legislatures
It requires a simple majority, the article being procedural in character
It cannot be amended at all, being the source of the amending power
expl: The amending article is itself among the provisions requiring ratification.
why: The fourth option states a proposition that was argued and rejected, which is why it retains an air of plausibility.
trapnote: The amending article is expressly among the entrenched provisions requiring ratification.

q: Consider the sequence: 1-A 1967 decision barred amendment of fundamental rights. 2-A 1971 amendment reversed it. 3-A 1973 decision restored the 1967 position. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The 1973 decision overruled the 1967 one and substituted a different limit.
why: The third statement is a plausible simplification and is the planted defect in the sequence.
trapnote: The 1973 decision did not restore the earlier bar. It imposed a different and narrower limit.

q: A State legislature passes a resolution for creation of a Legislative Council and Parliament does not act. Which statement is correct?
options: The Council comes into existence on the expiry of six months from the resolution
The Council comes into existence once the Governor notifies the resolution
No Council comes into existence; a fresh resolution must be passed every year
No Council comes into existence; the resolution is a precondition and not the operative act
expl: Parliament's law is the operative act in both creation and abolition.
why: The fourth option reaches the right conclusion by inventing a procedural requirement that does not exist.
trapnote: The Assembly proposes; Parliament disposes. Nothing happens until Parliament legislates.

q: Consider: 1-The 2018 amendment inserted a provision on the identification of backward classes. 2-A 2021 decision read it as removing the States' power. 3-A 2021 amendment restored that power. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are accurate and form a single cause-and-effect chain.
why: Two amendments three years apart on the same subject usually have a judicial decision between them.
trapnote: Amendment, decision, corrective amendment. Look for the decision whenever two amendments cluster.

q: On the maximum strength of the lower House, which statement is correct?
options: 552, comprising not more than 530 from States and 22 from Union Territories
550, comprising not more than 530 from States and 20 from Union Territories
545, comprising not more than 525 from States and 20 from Union Territories
550, comprising not more than 520 from States and 30 from Union Territories
expl: 530 plus 20 gives the present ceiling of 550.
why: Each wrong option alters one component, so the candidate must know the breakdown rather than the total.
trapnote: Learn the components. A total can be checked against them; a remembered total cannot.

q: Consider a constitutional amendment that abolishes judicial review of legislative action. Which statement is correct?
options: It is liable to be struck down, judicial review being part of the basic structure
It is valid, Parliament's amending power extending to any provision
It is valid if ratified by not less than half the State legislatures
It is liable to be struck down only if it also affects fundamental rights
expl: Judicial review is a recognised basic feature and cannot be removed by amendment.
why: The third option assumes that compliance with procedure cures a substantive defect, which it does not.
trapnote: Procedural compliance does not cure a basic-structure violation. The two checks are independent.

q: A candidate is told that the 2023 reservation amendment, the 2019 economic reservation and the 2020 seat extension are all currently operative. Which statement is correct?
options: All three are operative, the 2023 amendment having received assent
Only the 2019 amendment is operative, the other two awaiting further steps
Two of the three are operative; the 2020 amendment awaits a delimitation
Two of the three are operative; the 2023 amendment awaits a census and delimitation
expl: The 2019 and 2020 amendments operate; the 2023 amendment does not yet.
why: The fourth option identifies the right number of operative amendments and the wrong one as pending.
trapnote: Counting correctly is not enough. Identify which specific amendment is still pending.
